scope: R162 audit-disabled diagnostic: what the 155 Half checks cost in the harness
attribution: RESOLVED: the 34.7 ms activation region is the safety audit, not the MLP arithmetic
why_it_was_missed: the audit hook is registered on .mlp.fc1, .qkv_proj and .adaln_proj.linear, and its fc1 hook fires exactly at the E1 boundary of the span probe, so its scan time landed inside the fc1-to-fc2 interval. With the scan disabled the region collapses to 3.526 ms, which matches the 3.24 ms standalone measurement of the same operators.
what_the_audit_costs: each of the 155 audited calls materialises non-finite masks over a large FP16 tensor, sums them, and counts exact 65504 values: several full passes over up to 300 MB per call. Deferring the host readback (R161) did not help because the cost is the device-side scan, not the device-to-host copy.
implication_for_reported_numbers: the 17.9 to 18.1 s step measured so far, and therefore the 19.37 s and 20.03 s figures in the objective, all include about 2.87 s of verification scaffolding. The model itself runs at about 15.0 s per step in this configuration.
candidate_shape: keep all 155 checks but implement them far more cheaply: for an FP16 tensor the boundary condition is equivalent to max(abs(x)) reaching 65504, and finiteness can be tested with a nan/inf reduction, so two reductions replace the mask materialisation. Equivalence has to be argued and proven per condition before use.
honest_limit: this does not remove the checks, which the contract requires. It replaces a slow implementation with a cheap equivalent one, and the checks stay in the validated loop.

feasibility_update.note: with the audit cost separated out, 15.035 s minus a 2x FA kernel (3.80 s) and the linears at their measured standalone rates (2.26 s) lands at 8.98 s, so the 10 s target no longer needs the extra overhead reductions that the earlier 18.03 s arithmetic demanded
